# Optional built-in enhancement

**Status:** Proposed v0.1.8 direction  
**Scope:** Evidence-backed Extractions and Observations generated by the pinned Fieldnotes engine

## Product boundary

Enhancement is an optional, derived layer over the current notebook. It may recover literal evidence from Notes and synthesize narrow, reviewable patterns from cited evidence. It never changes, replaces, summarizes over, or becomes a prerequisite for a canonical Note.

A fresh installation has enhancement disabled. `fieldnotes sync`, local inspection, deterministic graph rebuild, merge, and ordinary notebook use must work without model assets, a GPU, an enhancement account, or hidden probabilistic behavior. Enabling enhancement is an explicit user action and any asset installation or download is separately visible.

Fieldnotes v0.1.8 uses only the engine, model assets, prompts/contracts, and generator versions selected and tested as part of the Fieldnotes release. It exposes no bring-your-own provider surface: no configurable provider, endpoint, hosted-model API key, model name, prompt, extractor plugin, or inference pipeline. Users who need other inference systems consume the notebook externally.

The exact engine, library/process shape, model asset packaging, download mechanism, supported languages, license, and resource envelope remain decisions for the 0.1.8 approval package. Those choices do not weaken the file and evidence rules in this document.

## Current-state and rebuild semantics

Extractions and Observations are separate public Markdown files while present, under `extractions/` and `observations/`. They are disposable current-state projections:

- deleting either directory leaves all Notes and retained artifacts unchanged;
- `enhancement rebuild` may delete and regenerate files from current evidence;
- a Note update or deletion invalidates derived records whose evidence no longer matches;
- stale records are removed or regenerated rather than retained as an enhancement history;
- v0.1 has no ledger of prior transcripts, model candidates, superseded Extractions, or superseded Observations;
- generator identifiers and versions explain current output but do not promise bit-for-bit identical probabilistic generation forever.

The same current Notes, pinned generator contract, model assets, deterministic settings, and platform should produce stable results to the degree practical. Any remaining variation is visible in separately versioned derived files, never hidden by mutating Notes.

## Extraction

An **Extraction** recovers structured evidence already present in exactly one Note but not supplied as reliable structured source metadata.

Appropriate Extraction capabilities include:

- voice transcription tied to audio time ranges;
- literal name, role, organization, email, phone, address, or URL values present in a signature or document;
- signature boundaries and separation from quoted history or disclaimers;
- literal salutation, sign-off, language, or address form for one interaction;
- invoice, purchase-order, contract, project, ticket, case, or document references;
- literal location or address evidence.

Syntax-led deterministic normalization remains core behavior. Values such as source-supplied identities, validated email/phone syntax, URLs, hashes, and timestamps do not become Extractions merely to route them through a model.

An Extraction:

- cites exactly one existing `source_note_id`;
- records an `ext_...` ID, derived type, `generated_at`, and `generator_version`;
- uses RFC 3339 datetimes with an explicit numeric offset, such as `2026-08-22T12:02:14+02:00`;
- carries exact text spans or audio time ranges wherever the value comes from text or audio;
- preserves literal recovered values rather than silently replacing them with inferred enrichment;
- may include a readable Markdown explanation or timecoded transcript body;
- obeys the notebook's flat scalar/list, stable-property, no-secret, and deterministic-serialization rules.

The precise Extraction filename convention and final public property registry remain fixture decisions. Filenames must contain the globally unique Extraction ID and be collision-safe.

## Exact text evidence validation

Text evidence is measured against the deterministic normalized Markdown body of the cited current Note—not a vendor payload, an unrecorded prompt input, or a later re-rendering.

Before 0.1.8 compatibility is claimed, the evidence coordinate system must be frozen with golden fixtures, including whether offsets count UTF-8 bytes, Unicode scalar values, or another explicit unit. This document does not choose that still-open encoding detail.

Regardless of the chosen unit, deterministic validation must confirm:

1. the cited Note exists and is the current Note version used by the generator;
2. every range is syntactically valid, finite, ordered, and inside the normalized body bounds;
3. slicing the body at that range yields the literal evidence claimed, under the approved normalization contract;
4. a range does not point only into frontmatter, hidden prompt material, or content absent from the Note body;
5. all required ranges refer to the one cited source Note;
6. property names and values conform to the approved flat derived-record registry;
7. evidence invalidated by a later Note rewrite is rejected or rebuilt, never presented as current.

Nonexistent ranges, approximate locations represented as exact, literal values that do not match their ranges, missing Note references, and stale body coordinates are rejected. Structured model output is useful input to this validator; it is not the safety boundary.

## Exact audio evidence validation

Audio evidence cites an audio artifact referenced by the current source Note and uses explicit start/end time ranges, conceptually such as `audio:12.400-18.250`.

Deterministic validation confirms:

1. the Note exists and references the claimed audio artifact;
2. the artifact exists, has an approved audio media type, and has a known or deterministically measured duration;
3. start and end are finite, non-negative, and use the approved time unit/precision;
4. start is strictly before end and the range lies within the artifact duration, subject only to an approved numeric tolerance;
5. transcript segments and extracted values cite the range that supports them;
6. ranges are bound to the current artifact bytes, not only a mutable input path;
7. a replaced or removed artifact invalidates its derived evidence.

The exact time precision, tolerance, segment-overlap policy, and transcript body layout remain golden-fixture decisions. Impossible time ranges, missing artifacts, wrong media, or unattached audio are rejected.

The original voice Note remains playable and useful when enhancement is disabled or all derived files are deleted.

## Observation

An **Observation** is a bounded interpretation or synthesis supported by one or more current Notes or Extractions. The evidence need not contain the conclusion as one literal string, but a reviewer must be able to follow the conclusion from the cited material.

Appropriate Observations include:

- repeated extracted sign-offs support a usual sign-off;
- explicit signature evidence plus deterministic identity evidence supports a likely organization affiliation;
- several damaged threads likely belong to one conversation;
- common participants, explicit references, and nearby instants support a candidate activity cluster;
- language counts across cited interactions support a usual or preferred interaction language under a documented rule;
- repeated literal address forms support a preferred interaction address form under an explicit rule;
- recurring exact references suggest a review candidate for cross-source identity resolution.

An Observation:

- records an `obs_...` ID, derived type, explicit-offset `generated_at`, and `generator_version`;
- cites existing Notes and/or Extractions through `supported_by` or the approved equivalent;
- identifies its subject entity when applicable;
- includes enough human-readable reasoning, counts, and time range to audit the conclusion;
- states ambiguity, conflicts, and bounded confidence where meaningful;
- uses only flat scalar/list frontmatter and readable Markdown;
- does not automatically merge entities or convert a candidate string into an established entity.

Purely deterministic results—exact identity matches, duplicate hashes, source-provided relationships, first/last seen instants, and interaction counts—remain deterministic graph facts. They do not require Observations.

## Observation evidence validation

Deterministic post-generation validation confirms:

- every cited Note or Extraction exists and is current;
- every cited Extraction already passed its exact source-evidence validation;
- all subject and evidence IDs use the expected record kinds;
- counts, date ranges, and literal categories in the explanation can be recomputed from the cited current evidence where the Observation claims an aggregate;
- the conclusion is inside an approved Observation capability and property registry;
- confidence, when present, is finite, bounded, and never used as a substitute for evidence;
- conflicting cited evidence is retained and disclosed;
- no cited instant is serialized without an explicit RFC 3339 offset.

An Observation with missing evidence, unreproducible counts, unsupported properties, dangling entities, or a prohibited judgment is rejected. A plausible sentence is not enough.

## Evidence origin in the graph

Validated Extractions and Observations may contribute `extracted` and `observed` claims to disposable entity and relationship projections. They do not bypass deterministic resolution:

- an extracted email may be normalized and matched under the approved email rule;
- an extracted organization name remains unresolved until a deterministic alias, domain, source identity, or approved user decision matches it;
- an Observation may create a review candidate but may not silently union entities;
- removing enhancement files and rebuilding removes their projected claims while retaining all deterministic graph facts.

Every projection retains its origin class and derived-record evidence IDs.

## Prohibited enhancement output

Enhancement may not generate or materialize:

- sentiment labels;
- relationship strength, trust, friendliness, or strategic importance;
- customer health, churn risk, lead score, opportunity quality, or priority;
- personality, psychological state, private preference, or intent;
- seniority or influence judgments beyond preserving a literal source role/title;
- claims that a person is a lead, customer, owner, or decision-maker unless merely preserving an explicit source-system fact under its source-specific vocabulary;
- unsupported identity merges or organization affiliations;
- proposed or executed external writes without separately cited evidence and the Fieldnotes handback boundary;
- model-generated summaries that replace available canonical source content;
- facts guessed from world knowledge rather than present, cited notebook evidence.

Source-explicit business values such as Jira priority may remain on a Note under the approved source/shared vocabulary. Enhancement must not assign those values itself.

The governing rule is:

> Extraction requires exact source presence. Observation requires cited, reviewable evidence.

Anything broader belongs to a downstream consumer.

## Engine, installation, and privacy boundary

The 0.1.8 approval package must select one release-owned engine configuration and document:

- engine and model versions;
- model and dependency licenses;
- supported languages and evidence-quality benchmarks;
- CPU, memory, disk, and optional accelerator requirements;
- whether assets are bundled, explicitly downloaded on enable, or installed as a separate optional package;
- offline behavior after installation;
- deterministic settings and known reproducibility limits;
- sandbox/process boundary and failure isolation;
- what content is processed and confirmation that credentials are excluded.

Normal `sync` never auto-enables enhancement or downloads weights. Engine logs, diagnostics, temporary files, and model inputs obey the same no-secret and damage-reporting rules as the rest of Fieldnotes. Failed enhancement leaves canonical Notes unchanged and produces no valid-looking partial derived file.

No user-configurable hosted inference endpoint or provider credential is part of v0.1.8.

## 0.1.8 acceptance direction

The optional enhancement increment is coherent when all of the following are demonstrated:

- a fresh install reports enhancement disabled and all deterministic product paths work without model assets;
- enable/install is explicit, reports license and resource requirements, and can be reversed;
- common approved voice formats produce transcripts whose time ranges pass deterministic validation;
- approved text capabilities produce literal values whose spans match exact normalized Note content;
- Observations cite current evidence, expose recomputable counts/time ranges where applicable, and retain ambiguity;
- invalid text spans, impossible audio ranges, missing records/artifacts, stale Note versions, wrong property types, and prohibited judgments are rejected;
- Extractions and Observations are separate, flat, human-readable Markdown files with explicit-offset datetimes and pinned generator provenance;
- canonical Notes and artifacts are byte-for-byte unchanged by enhancement and enhancement rebuild;
- deleting all enhancement files leaves a complete deterministic notebook and graph, and rebuilding restores only current supported projections;
- no provider/model/prompt selection or bring-your-own inference surface exists;
- supported-language, evidence-precision, resource, licensing, packaging, security, and cross-platform thresholds approved for the release are met;
- failures and interruptions leave no valid-looking partial derived records and never advance unrelated sync checkpoints.

The exact engine choice and final derived fixtures still require user approval. The 0.1.8 implementation may build validators and fixture-driven contracts before integrating the engine, but it is not complete until the pinned built-in engine passes the acceptance suite.
